slots.clue: Outpatient point: antiseizure drug with nonlinear kinetics and a high protein binding
slots.rationale: This drug small dose changes cause large level changes near the therapeutic range. Low albumin raises the free fraction.

slots.clue: ST elevation with symptoms is an emergency transfer, not a clinic observation
slots.rationale: Door-to-balloon time is the systems goal.

slots.clue: Flushing and red papules on the cheeks of an adult are This finding, not acne
slots.rationale: Triggers include heat and alcohol.

slots.clue: A young person with chest pain, a high troponin, and a recent virus may have This finding
slots.rationale: Supportive care and avoiding exercise are typical early advice.

slots.clue: A firm transilluminating wrist lump that changes size is usually a This finding
slots.rationale: Observation is reasonable when it does not limit function.

slots.clue: Outpatient point: azole antifungal for candida that inhibits CYP enzymes
slots.rationale: This drug raises levels of warfarin, some statins, and phenytoin. A one-time dose treats uncomplicated vaginal candida.

slots.clue: Outpatient point: anticonvulsant for neuropathic pain that is renally cleared and sedating
slots.rationale: This drug is titrated. Misuse and respiratory depression with opioids are current warnings.

slots.clue: Periumbilical bruising is an emergency finding, not a bruise from a belt
slots.rationale: This finding sign is associated with hemorrhagic pancreatitis.

slots.clue: Pregnancy and alcohol use are common settings
slots.rationale: Replace folate, but do not miss B12.

slots.clue: Outpatient point: therapeutic index small enough that levels or close monitoring are required
slots.rationale: Narrow therapeutic index drugs include warfarin, lithium, phenytoin, and digoxin.

slots.clue: Outpatient point: nK1 antagonist for delayed chemotherapy nausea that interacts with CYP3A4
slots.rationale: This drug can change the dose needs of dexamethasone and hormonal contraceptives.

slots.clue: Outpatient point: concentration drawn just before the next dose
slots.rationale: Aminoglycoside and vancomycin troughs, or AUC, are used to limit toxicity.

slots.clue: Manual muscle test graded from zero to five
slots.rationale: Manual muscle testing needs a standardized position. A grade of three is full range against gravity.

slots.clue: Distraction force used for some cervical and lumbar pain
slots.rationale: Traction is contraindicated in instability, infection, and severe osteoporosis. The first session is modest.

slots.clue: Weight-bearing rotation test for a meniscus tear
slots.rationale: The Thessaly test is done on one leg at slight knee flexion. Pain or locking suggests a meniscus lesion.

slots.clue: Nerve of the extensors, injured in the spiral groove
slots.rationale: Radial nerve injury causes wrist drop. Sensation is lost in the dorsal first web space.

slots.clue: Cranial nerve XI, trapezius and sternocleidomastoid
slots.rationale: Accessory nerve testing is a shoulder shrug and head turn. Neck dissection can injure it.

slots.clue: Slip of the femoral epiphysis in an adolescent, often with a limp
slots.rationale: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is an urgent orthopedic problem. The child may have knee pain only.

slots.clue: Cervical compression with extension and rotation for radiculopathy
slots.rationale: Spurling reproduces arm pain when a foramen is narrowed. It is not a screen to do vigorously.

slots.clue: Test of radial and ulnar artery patency in the hand
slots.rationale: The Allen test occludes both arteries, then releases one. Delayed blush means that artery is not adequate alone.

slots.clue: Ligament that stops anterior tibial translation
slots.rationale: The anterior cruciate ligament is tested by Lachman. Noncontact pivoting is a common tear mechanism.

slots.clue: Pain from nerve injury, often burning or electric
slots.rationale: Neuropathic pain is treated differently from inflammatory pain. Descriptors and sensory maps guide the exam.

slots.clue: Horizontal adductor and internal rotator of the shoulder
slots.rationale: Pectoralis major is lateral and medial pectoral nerves. Tightness limits external rotation.

slots.clue: Improvement from expectation and context, which is real but not the sole plan
slots.rationale: Placebo effects exist. They are not a reason to offer an inert treatment as if it were specific.

slots.clue: Order that allows the foot to touch for balance but not to take weight
slots.rationale: Toe-touch weight bearing is for balance. A scale can teach the patient what zero to slight pressure feels like.

slots.clue: Test for hip flexor tightness with the opposite knee held to the chest
slots.rationale: A Thomas test is positive when the thigh rises off the table. A abducted thigh also suggests IT-band tightness.

slots.clue: Distance between the feet
slots.rationale: A wide base is a balance compensation. A very narrow base is not stable after vestibular loss.

slots.clue: Visual or numeric scale of pain intensity
slots.rationale: A pain scale is one data point. Function and irritability matter as much as the number.

slots.clue: Finger flexor of the proximal interphalangeal joints, median innervated
slots.rationale: Flexor digitorum superficialis flexes the PIP joints. It is tested with the other fingers held extended.

slots.clue: Sense of joint position, lost in dorsal column and peripheral nerve disease
slots.rationale: Proprioception is tested by toe position and Romberg. It is required for balance when vision is removed.

slots.clue: Pain in the middle of abduction that eases near full elevation
slots.rationale: A painful arc suggests subacromial compression. Pain only at the end range is more acromioclavicular.

slots.clue: Sensory electrical stimulation used for pain
slots.rationale: Conventional TENS uses a comfortable tingling. It is not a strengthening current.

slots.clue: Electrical stimulation that produces a muscle contraction
slots.rationale: NMES is used for re-education and strengthening. It is not placed over a thrombus or the carotid sinus.

slots.clue: Nerve compressed at the cubital tunnel or Guyon canal
slots.rationale: Ulnar nerve injury weakens intrinsics and sensation of the ulnar one and a half digits.

slots.clue: Inferior traction test for multidirectional shoulder instability
slots.rationale: A sulcus sign is a visible gap under the acromion when the arm is pulled down.

slots.clue: Prone compression-rotation test for the meniscus
slots.rationale: Apley compression loads the meniscus. Distraction that hurts more suggests a ligament rather than the meniscus.

slots.clue: Neck muscle that tilts to the same side and rotates to the opposite side
slots.rationale: Sternocleidomastoid is accessory-nerve innervated. A tight left SCM tilts left and rotates right.

slots.clue: Diagonal patterns that use stronger muscles to facilitate weaker ones
slots.rationale: Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation uses spiral patterns, rhythmic stabilization, and contract-relax.

slots.clue: Short accelerating steps of Parkinson disease
slots.rationale: Festinating gait has a forward trunk and difficulty stopping. Cueing and larger steps are treatment targets.

slots.clue: Sensation that the knee will buckle, seen with ACL tears and quad inhibition
slots.rationale: Giving way after a pivot is an ACL story. Quad shutdown after swelling can feel the same.

slots.clue: Electrical stimulation timed to a functional task such as a step
slots.rationale: Functional electrical stimulation assists a weak muscle during the activity, such as dorsiflexion in swing.

slots.clue: Gait that shortens stance time on the painful limb
slots.rationale: An antalgic gait is a limp that unloads pain. The swing of the opposite limb is shortened.

slots.clue: Soft-tissue technique that is not performed over a known clot or acute infection
slots.rationale: Massage moves fluid and reduces guarding. It does not break up scar in a literal sense and is avoided over DVT.

slots.clue: Otolith organ that senses horizontal linear acceleration
slots.rationale: The utricle and saccule sense gravity and linear motion. They are not the spinning sensors.

slots.clue: Cervical test that relieves radicular pain when positive
slots.rationale: Manual distraction that eases arm pain supports a compressive radiculopathy.

slots.clue: Ankle-brachial index that screens for peripheral artery disease
slots.rationale: An ABI below about 0.9 suggests arterial disease. A very high value can mean calcified, incompressible vessels.

slots.clue: Double vision from misaligned eyes
slots.rationale: Diplopia that is new is a cranial nerve or neuromuscular problem until sorted out. Covering either eye clears binocular double vision.

slots.clue: Shoulder extender and internal rotator innervated by the thoracodorsal nerve
slots.rationale: Latissimus dorsi is the muscle of a pull-up and of crutch depression. The nerve is C6 to C8.

slots.clue: Sensitization in which pain persists after tissues have had time to heal
slots.rationale: Central sensitization is a processing problem. Hurt does not always mean fresh harm.

slots.clue: Test that extends the great toe to tighten the plantar fascia
slots.rationale: The windlass test reproduces heel pain in plantar fasciitis.

slots.clue: Scapular elevator and upward rotator innervated by cranial nerve XI
slots.rationale: Upper trapezius shrugs the shoulder. Weakness limits upward rotation needed for full flexion.

slots.clue: Reflex that keeps the eyes stable when the head turns
slots.rationale: The vestibulo-ocular reflex is impaired in vestibular hypofunction. Head-impulse testing checks it.

slots.clue: Freezing of gait, often in doorways, in Parkinson disease
slots.rationale: Freezing of gait responds to cueing, not to being pulled forward. Turns are practiced wide.

slots.clue: Horizontal adduction test for the acromioclavicular joint
slots.rationale: Cross-body adduction pain at the top of the shoulder suggests AC joint arthropathy.

slots.clue: Tibial tubercle apophysitis in growing athletes
slots.rationale: Osgood-Schlatter disease is traction on the tibial tubercle. Activity is modified, not usually operated.

slots.clue: Side-lying test for iliotibial band tightness
slots.rationale: The Ober test lets the top leg drop into adduction. Failure to drop means a tight IT band.

slots.clue: Inability to perform a learned movement despite intact strength
slots.rationale: Apraxia is a planning problem. Strength and sensation can be normal.

slots.clue: Rehab that uses habituation, gaze stability, and balance for inner-ear loss
slots.rationale: Vestibular rehabilitation is for unilateral hypofunction and BPPV. Gaze stability exercises are dosed so symptoms rise briefly then settle.

slots.clue: Light therapy used for pain and tissue healing in some protocols
slots.rationale: Low-level laser is not a thermal ultrasound. Eyes are protected, and it is not used over malignancy.

slots.clue: Sensory loss in the perineum, a cauda equina warning
slots.rationale: Saddle anesthesia is asked about and, when present with retention, referred urgently.

slots.clue: Positional test for posterior canal benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
slots.rationale: The Dix-Hallpike test hangs the head back and rotated. A brief upbeating torsional nystagmus supports posterior-canal BPPV.

slots.clue: Upper trunk brachial plexus injury, waiter's-tip posture
slots.rationale: Erb palsy is C5 to C6. The arm hangs internally rotated with the elbow extended.

slots.clue: Precautions after open heart surgery that limit pushing and pulling
slots.rationale: Sternal precautions protect the healing sternum. Transfers avoid a strong unilateral push.

slots.clue: Nerve compressed in carpal tunnel syndrome
slots.rationale: Median nerve injury at the wrist weakens the thenar muscles and sensation of the radial three and a half digits.

slots.clue: Swallowing difficulty that raises aspiration risk after stroke
slots.rationale: Dysphagia screening happens before oral intake after stroke. A wet voice or cough with water is a warning.

slots.clue: Cord syndrome of the older adult with more arm than leg weakness
slots.rationale: Central cord syndrome often follows hyperextension in cervical stenosis. Hands are weaker than legs.

slots.clue: Deep vein clot suspected with calf swelling, and a reason to hold aggressive massage
slots.rationale: Suspected DVT is not massaged or vigorously ranged until it is excluded. Sudden dyspnea suggests embolism.

slots.clue: Sudden block to extension, classically from a bucket-handle meniscus tear
slots.rationale: True locking is a mechanical block. Pseudolocking from pain is different.

slots.clue: Joint at the top of the shoulder separated in a fall on the point of the shoulder
slots.rationale: Acromioclavicular separations are graded by ligament injury. Cross-body adduction reproduces the pain.

slots.clue: Tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus, ruptured in a push-off injury
slots.rationale: Achilles rupture has a positive Thompson test. Tendinopathy is overload, not always inflammation.

slots.clue: Finding such as night pain, weight loss, or bowel change that needs medical review
slots.rationale: Red flags are not automatic serious disease, but they stop a routine musculoskeletal plan until they are addressed.

slots.clue: Kneading massage stroke
slots.rationale: Petrissage lifts and kneads muscle. Pressure stays within tolerance and avoids bony prominences.

slots.clue: Wrist extensor commonly involved in lateral epicondylalgia
slots.rationale: Extensor carpi radialis brevis attaches at the lateral epicondyle. It extends and radially deviates the wrist.

slots.clue: Maneuver that tests whether an infant hip can be dislocated
slots.rationale: Barlow is a provocation test. A clunk is referred, not stretched in therapy.

slots.clue: Medial scapular lift from serratus or trapezius weakness
slots.rationale: Serratus winging is worse with forward flexion. Trapezius winging is worse with abduction.

slots.clue: Historical calf-pain sign that is not reliable for deep vein thrombosis
slots.rationale: Homans sign is not used to rule a clot in or out. Swelling and a risk score matter more.

slots.clue: High-volt pulsed current used for wound healing polarity protocols
slots.rationale: High-voltage current can be set to attract or repel cells in wound care. Polarity protocols differ by wound stage.

slots.clue: Passive stretch of the wrist extensors for lateral epicondylalgia
slots.rationale: The Mill test pronates the forearm and flexes the wrist. Pain at the lateral epicondyle is positive.

slots.clue: Ligament that stops posterior tibial translation
slots.rationale: The posterior cruciate ligament is injured by a dashboard blow. Posterior drawer and sag test it.

slots.clue: Impingement test that passively flexes the internally rotated arm
slots.rationale: Neer test pain is subacromial. It does not by itself prove a rotator cuff tear.

slots.clue: Increased thoracic curve
slots.rationale: Excess kyphosis shifts the center of mass forward. Osteoporotic wedge fractures are one cause.

slots.clue: Rating of perceived exertion used to dose aerobic exercise
slots.rationale: RPE is the guide when medications blunt heart rate. Moderate work is the middle of the scale.

slots.clue: Wrist flexion test for carpal tunnel syndrome
slots.rationale: Phalen holds the wrists flexed. Numbness in the median distribution is a positive test.

slots.clue: Scapular elevator innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve
slots.rationale: Levator scapulae elevates the superior angle. It is often tight with a forward head.

slots.clue: Thumb flexor innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve
slots.rationale: Flexor pollicis longus flexes the thumb IP joint. Anterior interosseous palsy loses that and the index DIP.

slots.clue: Drawer test that assesses the PCL with the knee flexed
slots.rationale: A posterior sag of the tibia at 90 degrees also suggests PCL injury.

slots.clue: Phase when the foot is off the ground
slots.rationale: Swing needs hip flexion, knee flexion, and dorsiflexion to clear the foot.

slots.clue: Resisted wrist extension test for lateral epicondylalgia
slots.rationale: Cozen reproduces pain at the lateral epicondyle. It loads extensor carpi radialis brevis.

slots.clue: Cranial nerve XII, motor to the tongue
slots.rationale: Hypoglossal injury deviates the tongue to the weak side on protrusion.

slots.clue: Flat foot, which may be flexible or from posterior tibial tendon failure
slots.rationale: Flexible pes planus forms an arch when non-weight-bearing. Adult acquired flatfoot is a tibialis posterior problem.

slots.clue: Disabilities of the arm, shoulder, and hand questionnaire
slots.rationale: The DASH captures upper-limb function in daily tasks. It is used across many shoulder and elbow diagnoses.

slots.clue: Scan that measures bone mineral density
slots.rationale: DEXA results are reported as T-scores. Therapy still focuses on strength, posture, and fall risk.

slots.clue: Machine that moves a joint through a set range after some surgeries
slots.rationale: Continuous passive motion does not replace active exercise. The range is progressed by the surgeon's limits.

slots.clue: Lifting the pelvis to clear a swing foot that will not flex
slots.rationale: Hip hiking compensates for weak hip flexors or dorsiflexors.

slots.clue: Timed test of rising, walking three meters, and returning
slots.rationale: The Timed Up and Go over a community cutoff suggests fall risk. The conditions of the test are kept standard.

slots.clue: Knee test for ACL integrity, preferred in the acute setting over the anterior drawer
slots.rationale: Lachman is done at about 20 degrees of flexion. A soft end feel suggests an ACL tear.

slots.clue: Inward curve of the cervical or lumbar spine
slots.rationale: Excess lumbar lordosis loads the facets. A flat lumbar spine can follow flexion-biased pain.

slots.clue: Active compression test used for SLAP and acromioclavicular pain
slots.rationale: O'Brien pain that is worse with the thumb down and better with the palm up is the classic pattern.

slots.clue: Pain from tissue threat, such as arthritis or a sprain
slots.rationale: Nociceptive pain is more local and mechanical. It usually fits the tissue healing timeline.

slots.clue: Neuropathic collapse of the foot in diabetes, which is hot and swollen
slots.rationale: Charcot foot is offloaded. It is distinguished from infection, which can coexist.

slots.clue: Two-joint quadriceps that also flexes the hip
slots.rationale: Rectus femoris is tight on the Ely test. It is the only quadriceps that crosses the hip.

slots.clue: Knee extensor innervated by the femoral nerve
slots.rationale: Quadriceps includes rectus femoris and the vasti. The reflex is L3 to L4.

slots.clue: Elbow flexor and supinator innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve
slots.rationale: The long head of biceps also depresses the humeral head. The reflex is C5 to C6.

slots.clue: Contraction without joint motion, used when motion is not yet allowed
slots.rationale: Isometrics maintain muscle when the joint must stay still. They can raise blood pressure if the breath is held.

slots.clue: Inpatient cardiac rehab started when the patient is stable
slots.rationale: Phase I cardiac rehab is early mobilization and education. Intensity stays low and symptoms are watched.

slots.clue: Contraction through a range with a constant external load
slots.rationale: Isotonic exercise includes concentric and eccentric phases. The load is progressed by repetition and weight.

slots.clue: Tremor that worsens as the hand nears the target
slots.rationale: Intention tremor is cerebellar. A resting tremor is Parkinson disease.

slots.clue: Lower trunk plexus injury affecting the hand intrinsics
slots.rationale: Klumpke palsy is C8 to T1. A claw hand and sometimes Horner syndrome are associated.

slots.clue: Capsulitis that limits external rotation early and then all motions
slots.rationale: Adhesive capsulitis has freezing, frozen, and thawing stages. External rotation is often lost first.

slots.clue: Scale that grades spasticity from none to rigid
slots.rationale: The Modified Ashworth Scale scores resistance to passive movement. It is used to track tone treatment.

slots.clue: Neck disability index, the cervical cousin of the Oswestry
slots.rationale: The Neck Disability Index is a patient-reported outcome. It does not replace the neurologic exam.

slots.clue: Strategy of doing activity in planned amounts rather than boom and bust
slots.rationale: Pacing prevents the cycle of overdoing and crashing. The quota is increased gradually.

slots.clue: Bone forming in soft tissue after trauma or surgery
slots.rationale: Heterotopic ossification limits motion. Aggressive passive stretch is not the treatment once it is forming.

slots.clue: Lower extremity functional scale
slots.rationale: The LEFS is a patient-reported score for hip, knee, and ankle problems. Higher is better function.

slots.clue: Finger flexor of the distal joints; the lateral half is median and the medial half ulnar
slots.rationale: Flexor digitorum profundus to the ring and little fingers is ulnar. The index and middle are anterior interosseous.

slots.clue: Support time when both feet are on the ground
slots.rationale: Double-limb support increases when balance is poor. It shortens as speed increases in healthy gait.

slots.clue: Sensory nerve along the lateral foot, often harvested as a graft
slots.rationale: The sural nerve is pure sensory. Numbness on the lateral foot follows its injury.

slots.clue: Stress test for the lateral collateral ligament
slots.rationale: Varus stress at 30 degrees tests the LCL. Opening in extension suggests posterolateral corner injury too.

slots.clue: Nerve of the plantarflexors and foot intrinsics
slots.rationale: Tibial nerve injury loses plantarflexion and toe flexion and sensation on the sole.

slots.clue: Injury from cold left on too long or over an insensate area
slots.rationale: Cold burns look like burns. Limit time and use a layer when sensation is poor.

slots.clue: Transient burner from a traction or compression injury of the upper trunk
slots.rationale: A stinger that clears quickly is observed. Lasting weakness is not returned to play.

slots.clue: Quick stretch-shorten exercise introduced late in rehab
slots.rationale: Plyometrics require a quiet joint and good strength first. Landings are taught before height is added.

slots.clue: End of stance when the foot leaves the ground
slots.rationale: Toe-off needs great-toe extension and plantarflexor power. Hallux limitus shortens this phase.

slots.clue: Wrist flexor innervated by the median nerve
slots.rationale: Flexor carpi radialis flexes and radially deviates the wrist. It is a median-innervated forearm muscle.

slots.clue: Bone death from lost blood supply, classically the femoral head
slots.rationale: Avascular necrosis causes deep joint pain. Early films can be normal.

slots.clue: Ligament injured first in a typical lateral ankle sprain
slots.rationale: The anterior talofibular ligament limits anterior translation of the talus. The anterior drawer tests it.

slots.clue: Debris in a semicircular canal that causes BPPV
slots.rationale: Canalithiasis produces a brief nystagmus. Cupulolithiasis lasts longer while the head is held in the provoking position.

slots.clue: Compression fracture of the posterolateral humeral head after anterior dislocation
slots.rationale: A Hill-Sachs lesion is seen after the humeral head impacts the glenoid. Large ones affect stability.

slots.clue: Seated neural tension test for the sciatic tract
slots.rationale: The slump test adds cervical flexion to a straight leg raise. Symptoms that ease when the neck is extended support neural tension.

slots.clue: Gait that moves the device and the opposite leg together
slots.rationale: A two-point gait resembles normal reciprocal walking. It is for patients who can take weight on both legs.

slots.clue: Primary muscle of inspiration, innervated by the phrenic nerve
slots.rationale: Diaphragmatic breathing emphasizes belly rise and less upper-chest use. The nerve roots are C3 to C5.

slots.clue: Fluid sac that inflames in front of the patella or at the pes anserinus
slots.rationale: Prepatellar bursitis follows kneeling. It is distinguished from a joint effusion, which is inside the capsule.

slots.clue: Constant resistance through the range, as in Parkinson disease
slots.rationale: Lead-pipe or cogwheel rigidity is basal ganglia. It does not depend on the speed of the passive movement the way spasticity does.

slots.clue: Pain questionnaire that captures quality, not only intensity
slots.rationale: The McGill Pain Questionnaire uses word lists. Burning and shooting language suggests neuropathic pain.

slots.clue: Pain from a stimulus that should not hurt
slots.rationale: Allodynia is a neuropathic feature. Light touch that hurts changes how manual therapy is dosed.

slots.clue: Quality of resistance at the end of passive motion
slots.rationale: A bony end feel is hard, a capsular end feel is firm, and a spasm end feel is guarding. An empty end feel is pain before resistance.

slots.clue: Neurodevelopmental approach that emphasizes normal movement and handling
slots.rationale: Bobath, or NDT, uses handling to reduce unwanted tone and guide functional movement.

slots.clue: Open-glottis forced expiration that moves secretions without a hard cough
slots.rationale: Huff coughing is used in COPD and cystic fibrosis. It is less tiring than stacked coughing.

slots.clue: Pain from an organ that can mimic a musculoskeletal problem
slots.rationale: Visceral pain is poorly localized and may come with nausea or a change in bowel or bladder. It is not stretched away.

slots.clue: Inattention to one side, usually the left after a right hemisphere stroke
slots.rationale: Unilateral neglect is not a visual field cut. Cueing and scanning practice are used.

slots.clue: Fluid inside the knee, tested by ballotment or a bulge sign
slots.rationale: A knee effusion can follow a meniscus tear, arthritis, or infection. A hot swollen knee with fever is urgent.

slots.clue: Performance test of balance and gait
slots.rationale: The Tinetti assessment scores sitting balance through gait. It is used for fall-risk decisions.

slots.clue: Lateral ankle ligament stressed by inversion in neutral
slots.rationale: The calcaneofibular ligament is injured after the ATFL in more severe inversion sprains.

slots.clue: Abductor innervated by the axillary nerve
slots.rationale: Deltoid takes over abduction after supraspinatus starts it. Axillary nerve injury follows shoulder dislocation.

slots.clue: Device held in the hand opposite the weak or painful leg
slots.rationale: A cane reduces load on the opposite hip. It advances with the involved limb.

slots.clue: Elevation in the plane of the scapula, used for cuff exercise
slots.rationale: Scaption is about 30 degrees forward of the frontal plane. It is a comfortable plane for supraspinatus loading.

slots.clue: Leg-raise test for lumbar nerve root irritation
slots.rationale: A straight leg raise that reproduces pain below the knee suggests radiculopathy, often L5 or S1.

slots.clue: Training that restrains the stronger arm to force use of the weaker arm
slots.rationale: Constraint-induced therapy requires some residual hand movement. It is intensive and task specific.

slots.clue: Compression of the IT band over the lateral femoral condyle
slots.rationale: The Noble test is positive for IT-band friction when pain occurs near 30 degrees of flexion.

slots.clue: Muscle that supinates with biceps and is pierced by the radial nerve deep branch
slots.rationale: The posterior interosseous nerve can be compressed in the supinator arcade of Frohse.

slots.clue: Single-limb support as the body moves over the foot
slots.rationale: Midstance requires hip abductor control to keep the pelvis level.

slots.clue: History that raises the chance back pain is not simple strain
slots.rationale: A history of cancer plus new spine pain is imaged according to medical guidance. It is not labeled mechanical by default.

slots.clue: Medial tibial stress pain in runners, a stress injury until proven otherwise
slots.rationale: Medial tibial stress syndrome is overuse. Focal bone tenderness raises concern for a stress fracture.

slots.clue: Flick of the middle finger that flexes the thumb, a cervical myelopathy sign
slots.rationale: A Hoffman sign suggests an upper motor neuron lesion, often cervical cord compression.

slots.clue: Postural plantarflexor tested with the knee bent
slots.rationale: Soleus is deep to gastrocnemius and is tibial innervated. It is the endurance calf muscle.

slots.clue: Ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis from sympathetic loss
slots.rationale: Horner syndrome with arm pain can mean an apical lung tumor. It is not a simple neck strain.

slots.clue: First step after injury so the tissue is not loaded past its tolerance
slots.rationale: Protection includes crutches, a brace, or rest. The grade of injury decides how much.

slots.clue: Small external rotator innervated by the axillary nerve
slots.rationale: Teres minor shares external rotation with infraspinatus. The axillary nerve also supplies deltoid.

slots.clue: Alignment screen of the spine and limbs in standing
slots.rationale: Posture findings are correlated with symptoms. A forward head is common and is not itself a diagnosis.

slots.clue: Inflammatory spine disease that fuses the spine in flexion if untreated
slots.rationale: Ankylosing spondylitis needs extension exercise and medical care. A fused spine fractures with minor trauma.

slots.clue: Coordination deficit from cerebellum or sensory loss
slots.rationale: Cerebellar ataxia includes dysmetria and intention tremor. Sensory ataxia worsens with the eyes closed.

slots.clue: Surgical fixation of a fracture with hardware
slots.rationale: Open reduction internal fixation has motion and weight-bearing limits. Hardware is not a reason to use diathermy over the site.

slots.clue: Percussion over a nerve that reproduces distal tingling
slots.rationale: Tinel at the carpal tunnel suggests median nerve irritation. It is also used at the tarsal tunnel and elbow.

slots.clue: Thenar muscle that abducts the thumb and is median innervated
slots.rationale: Abductor pollicis brevis is the muscle of thenar wasting in carpal tunnel syndrome.

slots.clue: Primary hip flexor from the iliacus and psoas
slots.rationale: Iliopsoas is femoral and lumbar innervated. It is the muscle of the Thomas test.

slots.clue: Muscle soreness a day or two after unaccustomed exercise
slots.rationale: Delayed-onset soreness is not acute injury. It follows eccentric work and resolves. Sharp joint pain is different.

slots.clue: Brain injury managed with relative rest and a graded return
slots.rationale: Concussion return follows a stepwise protocol. A second impact before recovery is the danger.

slots.clue: Velocity-dependent resistance from an upper motor neuron lesion
slots.rationale: Spasticity is not rigidity. It is faster when the limb is moved faster, and it is treated with stretch and sometimes baclofen.

slots.clue: Wide-based unsteady gait from cerebellar or sensory loss
slots.rationale: Ataxic gait is not the same as weakness. Look for dysmetria or a positive Romberg to sort the cause.

slots.clue: Burst alternating current used for strengthening
slots.rationale: Russian current is a strengthening protocol. The contraction is dosed like exercise, with rest intervals.

slots.clue: Rhythmic eye movement seen in vestibular disorders
slots.rationale: Peripheral nystagmus is often unidirectional and suppressed by fixation. Central nystagmus can be vertical.

slots.clue: Intersecting medium-frequency currents used for pain
slots.rationale: Interferential current is comfortable for larger areas. The beat frequency is the treatment frequency.

slots.clue: Angle from the ASIS to the patella to the tibial tubercle
slots.rationale: A larger Q angle is discussed in patellofemoral pain. It is not a stand-alone surgical indication.

slots.clue: Inability to adduct the little finger, an ulnar nerve sign
slots.rationale: Wartenberg sign is a persistently abducted fifth digit from interosseous weakness.

slots.clue: Wrist flexor innervated by the ulnar nerve
slots.rationale: Flexor carpi ulnaris is the ulnar wrist flexor. The ulnar nerve enters the forearm through its heads.

slots.clue: Protection, rest, ice, compression, and elevation for an acute sprain
slots.rationale: PRICE is the acute soft-tissue start. It is not the whole rehab, and ice is not used on insensate skin.

slots.clue: Metabolic equivalents used to describe the energy cost of a task
slots.rationale: One MET is resting oxygen use. Cardiac patients are progressed by MET level and symptoms.

slots.clue: Pattern that advances both crutches then brings the feet up to them
slots.rationale: Swing-to is used with bilateral devices when the legs cannot step through, as in some spinal cord gaits.

slots.clue: Pain that wakes the patient and does not ease with position, a reason to screen further
slots.rationale: Unrelenting night pain can be inflammatory, infectious, or malignant. Mechanical pain usually eases with a position change.

slots.clue: Angle measured on a radiograph to grade scoliosis
slots.rationale: The Cobb angle is the surgical and bracing language of scoliosis. Therapy does not replace that measurement.

slots.clue: Balance scale scored from sitting and standing tasks
slots.rationale: The Berg Balance Scale predicts fall risk. A lower score means more assistance is needed.

slots.clue: Questionnaire of low-back disability
slots.rationale: The Oswestry Disability Index turns pain and function into a percent disability. It tracks change, not imaging.

slots.clue: Deep heat from electromagnetic energy, kept away from metal and implants
slots.rationale: Short-wave diathermy is contraindicated with pacemakers and metal in the field. It heats large areas.

slots.clue: Pain between the metatarsal heads from an interdigital nerve
slots.rationale: Morton neuroma is often between the third and fourth toes. Squeeze of the forefoot reproduces it.

slots.clue: Hip flexor and knee flexor that is the longest muscle
slots.rationale: Sartorius is femoral innervated and forms the lateral border of the femoral triangle.

slots.clue: Forward-bend test for a rib hump in scoliosis
slots.rationale: The Adams test shows rotation. It is a screen, not a Cobb angle.

slots.clue: Theory that nonpainful input can reduce transmission of pain
slots.rationale: Gate control is one reason TENS and rubbing can help. It is not the only pain mechanism.

slots.clue: Exercise in which the foot or hand is fixed, such as a squat
slots.rationale: Closed-chain exercise uses co-contraction. It is often introduced early for the knee when weight bearing is allowed.

slots.clue: Display of muscle activity used to up-train or down-train a muscle
slots.rationale: Biofeedback shows the patient the contraction. It is a teaching tool, not a passive treatment.

slots.clue: Quick eye movement to a new target
slots.rationale: Saccades are tested for accuracy. Overshoot suggests a cerebellar problem.

slots.clue: Lateral knee ligament injured by a varus force
slots.rationale: The lateral collateral ligament is less often injured alone. Varus laxity in extension is a complex injury.

slots.clue: Upgoing toe with plantar stimulation, a sign of an upper motor neuron lesion
slots.rationale: Babinski is normal in infants. In adults it suggests corticospinal tract involvement.

slots.clue: Pattern of restriction typical of arthritis in a joint
slots.rationale: The shoulder capsular pattern limits external rotation most, then abduction, then internal rotation.

slots.clue: Compression of the lumbosacral roots with saddle anesthesia and bladder change
slots.rationale: Cauda equina syndrome is an emergency. Saddle sensory loss and urinary retention need urgent imaging.

slots.clue: Pain along the sciatic distribution, often from a lumbar disc
slots.rationale: Sciatica that is only back pain is not radiculopathy. True radicular pain goes below the knee.

slots.clue: Flexion, adduction, and internal rotation test for femoroacetabular impingement
slots.rationale: FADIR reproduces groin pain in cam or pincer impingement and in many labral tears.

slots.clue: Breath hold that spikes blood pressure during a lift
slots.rationale: Patients with cardiac disease are taught to exhale on effort so they do not perform a Valsalva maneuver.

slots.clue: Scale of perceived exertion from rest to maximal
slots.rationale: The Borg scale lets a patient report effort when a heart-rate formula is unreliable, as on a beta blocker.

slots.clue: Sesamoid in the quadriceps tendon that tracks in the trochlea
slots.rationale: Patellar tracking is influenced by the vastus medialis, IT band, and foot pronation.

slots.clue: Primary elbow flexor innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve
slots.rationale: Brachialis flexes the elbow in pronation and supination. It is deep to biceps.

slots.clue: Raising a limb above the heart to help swelling
slots.rationale: Elevation uses gravity. It is paired with movement of the distal joints when that is allowed.

slots.clue: Eyes-closed stance test for proprioception, not the cerebellum
slots.rationale: Romberg is positive when balance is lost only after the eyes close. Cerebellar ataxia is present with eyes open too.

slots.clue: Disc material that can compress a nerve root
slots.rationale: A lumbar herniation often hurts more in flexion and sitting. Most improve without surgery.

slots.clue: Canalith repositioning maneuver for posterior canal BPPV
slots.rationale: The Epley maneuver moves debris out of the posterior canal. It is not the treatment for central vertigo.

slots.clue: Rhythmic beats at the ankle from an upper motor neuron lesion
slots.rationale: Sustained clonus is pathologic. A beat or two can be normal if it stops quickly.

slots.clue: Rotation test for a meniscus tear, listening for a click with joint-line pain
slots.rationale: McMurray combines rotation and extension. It is not perfectly sensitive, so a negative test does not clear the meniscus.

slots.clue: Loading response after initial contact
slots.rationale: Foot flat is when the rest of the foot accepts weight. Knee flexion cushions this phase.

slots.clue: Paper-pinch test for ulnar nerve weakness of adductor pollicis
slots.rationale: Froment is positive when the thumb IP joint flexes to hold the paper, substituting flexor pollicis longus.

slots.clue: Lesion pattern with spasticity, hyperreflexia, and Babinski
slots.rationale: An upper motor neuron lesion is the brain or spinal cord. Tone is high and reflexes are brisk.

slots.clue: Pendulum exercise used early after shoulder surgery
slots.rationale: Codman pendulums use body sway, not active shoulder muscle. They are for mobility, not strengthening.

slots.clue: Cranial nerve X, motor to the palate and a voice nerve
slots.rationale: Vagus injury hoarsens the voice and can cause nasal regurgitation. It is tested with palate elevation.

slots.clue: Gliding massage stroke used to start and finish a session
slots.rationale: Effleurage is light and longitudinal. It is not the deep stroke.

slots.clue: Functional independence measure used in rehabilitation settings
slots.rationale: The FIM scores burden of care from dependent to independent. It is an outcome, not a diagnosis.

slots.clue: Elbow extensor innervated by the radial nerve
slots.rationale: Triceps reflex is C7. Radial nerve injury in the spiral groove spares the triceps if the branch has already left.

slots.clue: Prone knee flexion test for rectus femoris tightness
slots.rationale: Ely is positive when the hip flexes as the knee is flexed in prone.

slots.clue: Smooth eye tracking of a moving target
slots.rationale: Smooth pursuit is a central eye-movement skill. It is not a test of the peripheral labyrinth.

slots.clue: Nerve injured at the fibular head that causes foot drop
slots.rationale: Common fibular nerve injury spares inversion if tibialis posterior is intact, and loses eversion and dorsiflexion.

slots.clue: Contraction at a set speed on a dynamometer
slots.rationale: Isokinetic devices match resistance to the patient's effort at a chosen speed. They are used for testing and training.

slots.clue: Great toe; valgus is a bunion and rigidus is stiff arthritis
slots.rationale: Hallux valgus shifts the toe laterally. First MTP extension is needed for gait.

slots.clue: History that raises fracture and avascular necrosis risk
slots.rationale: Long steroid use weakens bone and can necrose the femoral head. A new groin pain in that patient is taken seriously.

slots.clue: Joint surface that glides opposite the bone swing
slots.rationale: A convex surface glides opposite the swing. The glenohumeral head glides inferiorly as the arm abducts.

slots.clue: A finding that means a modality or exercise is not used
slots.rationale: Contraindications are not preferences. Malignancy, pregnancy, and a pacemaker change what energy can be applied.

slots.clue: Supraspinatus test with the thumb down in the scapular plane
slots.rationale: The empty-can test loads supraspinatus. Weakness more than pain suggests a tear.

slots.clue: Stress test for the medial collateral ligament
slots.rationale: Valgus stress at 30 degrees isolates the MCL. Laxity in full extension implies a more complex injury.

slots.clue: Drawer test of the knee that also stresses the ACL, less sensitive acutely
slots.rationale: The anterior drawer is done at 90 degrees. Hamstring guarding can hide an ACL tear.

slots.clue: Device that encourages a sustained deep breath after surgery
slots.rationale: Incentive spirometry prevents atelectasis. The patient inhales slowly and holds.

slots.clue: Nerve of the anterior thigh that extends the knee and flexes the hip
slots.rationale: Femoral nerve injury loses knee extension and the patellar reflex. Sensation is lost on the anterior thigh and medial leg.

slots.clue: Inner-ear disease with vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus, and fullness
slots.rationale: Meniere episodes last hours, not seconds. Salt restriction and vestibular rehab are parts of care.

slots.clue: Walk test of endurance used in pulmonary and cardiac rehab
slots.rationale: The six-minute walk records distance, rests, and oxygen. It is a functional capacity measure.

slots.clue: Figure-four test for hip or sacroiliac irritation
slots.rationale: FABER is flexion, abduction, and external rotation. Groin pain points to the hip; posterior pain can be the SI joint.

slots.clue: Lesion pattern with flaccid weakness, hyporeflexia, and fasciculations
slots.rationale: A lower motor neuron lesion is the root or peripheral nerve. Atrophy and fasciculations point there.

slots.clue: Test in which the patient cannot slowly lower the arm, suggesting a cuff tear
slots.rationale: A positive drop-arm test implies a significant supraspinatus or cuff tear.

slots.clue: Slurred speech from weak or uncoordinated speech muscles
slots.rationale: Dysarthria spares language comprehension. It follows cranial nerve or cerebellar lesions.

slots.clue: Medial knee ligament injured by a valgus force
slots.rationale: The medial collateral ligament is tested at 30 degrees of flexion. Many isolated tears are treated without surgery.

slots.clue: Synovial fold that can snap at the medial patella
slots.rationale: A symptomatic plica is a diagnosis of exclusion. Medial overload and tracking are treated first.

slots.clue: Brief positional vertigo from canaliths in a semicircular canal
slots.rationale: BPPV lasts seconds, is triggered by rolling or looking up, and is treated with repositioning.

slots.clue: Normal opposite arm and leg pattern
slots.rationale: Reciprocal gait is the goal when both limbs can accept weight. Devices are weaned toward it.

slots.clue: Emergency cluster of saddle anesthesia and bladder change
slots.rationale: Cauda equina is referred the same day. Progressive leg weakness with urinary retention is not a wait-and-see back pain.

slots.clue: Goggles that remove fixation so vestibular nystagmus can be seen
slots.rationale: Frenzel or infrared goggles unmask peripheral nystagmus. Fixation can hide it.

slots.clue: Cartilage rim of the glenoid, torn in SLAP and Bankart lesions
slots.rationale: A Bankart lesion is an anterior-inferior labral tear with dislocation. A SLAP tear involves the biceps anchor.

slots.clue: Muscles that flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints
slots.rationale: The lateral two lumbricals are median and the medial two are ulnar. They balance the extrinsic flexors.

slots.clue: Cartilage that loads the knee and tears with twisting
slots.rationale: Meniscus tears cause joint-line pain, catching, and swelling. The outer third has a blood supply.

slots.clue: Weight loss with pain that is a medical red flag
slots.rationale: Unexplained weight loss is not a strengthening deficit. The patient is referred.

slots.clue: Contraction that shortens the muscle
slots.rationale: A concentric quadriceps contraction extends the knee against gravity or a weight.

slots.clue: Exhalation through pursed lips that slows breathing in COPD
slots.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing keeps small airways open longer and reduces air trapping.

slots.clue: Otolith organ that senses vertical linear acceleration
slots.rationale: The saccule is an otolith organ. The semicircular canals, not the saccule, sense rotation.

slots.clue: Principle that the body adapts specifically to the demand imposed
slots.rationale: SAID means a program must resemble the goal task. Strength on a machine does not automatically become sport skill.

slots.clue: Nerve from C3 to C5 that innervates the diaphragm
slots.rationale: Phrenic nerve injury impairs inspiration. C3 through C5 keep the diaphragm alive is the memory line.

slots.clue: Scapular protractor that prevents winging
slots.rationale: Serratus anterior is long thoracic innervated. Winging is more obvious when the arms push forward.

slots.clue: Test for the long head of biceps with the shoulder flexed against resistance
slots.rationale: Speed test pain is in the bicipital groove. It is used for biceps tendinopathy.

slots.clue: Joint surface that glides in the same direction as the bone swing
slots.rationale: The concave-convex rule says a concave surface glides with the osteokinematic motion.

slots.clue: Break in a bone that is protected until it can be loaded
slots.rationale: Fracture precautions come from the surgeon. Weight bearing status is an order, not a guess.

slots.clue: Cranial nerve IV, which depresses the adducted eye
slots.rationale: Trochlear palsy causes difficulty looking down the stairs. The head tilts away from the weak muscle.

slots.clue: Closed muscle space where swelling can stop perfusion
slots.rationale: Exertional compartment syndrome causes pain and paresthesia that resolve with rest. Acute compartment syndrome is an emergency.

slots.clue: Uncemented fixation that may limit early weight bearing
slots.rationale: Press-fit implants rely on bone ingrowth. Weight-bearing status is the surgeon's decision.

slots.clue: Quick head turn that shows a corrective saccade if the reflex is weak
slots.rationale: A positive head impulse suggests peripheral vestibular loss. A normal impulse in acute vertigo raises concern for stroke.

slots.clue: Behavior that pushes toward the weaker side after stroke
slots.rationale: Pusher syndrome is an altered sense of upright. The patient resists correction toward the strong side.

slots.clue: Pain from a nerve root that travels in a dermatome
slots.rationale: Radicular pain often goes below the knee or into the hand. Reflex and strength changes support it.

slots.clue: Bone density below normal but not yet in the osteoporosis range
slots.rationale: Osteopenia is a reason to load bone and to prevent falls, not a reason to stop exercise.

slots.clue: Chest pain from myocardial ischemia that stops exercise
slots.rationale: Angina during therapy means stop, rest, and follow the cardiac plan. It is not worked through.

slots.clue: Contraction that lengthens under load, used for tendinopathy
slots.rationale: Eccentric loading is a staple of Achilles and patellar tendinopathy programs. The muscle controls the lowering.

slots.clue: Medial thigh adductor that also flexes the knee
slots.rationale: Gracilis is an obturator-nerve muscle and a pes anserinus tendon.

slots.clue: Heart-rate reserve method for exercise intensity
slots.rationale: Karvonen uses resting heart rate plus a percent of the reserve. Beta blockers make the formula less valid.

slots.clue: Language impairment; Broca is nonfluent and Wernicke is fluent but empty
slots.rationale: Aphasia is cortical. Use yes-no and gestures. Dysarthria is a speech-motor problem, not a language problem.

slots.clue: Anterior-inferior labral tear associated with anterior dislocation
slots.rationale: Bankart repair restores the anterior labrum. The Hill-Sachs lesion is the companion humeral head impression.

slots.clue: Nerve of deltoid and teres minor, injured in anterior shoulder dislocation
slots.rationale: Axillary nerve injury loses abduction and sensation over the lateral shoulder.

slots.clue: High arch associated with neurologic disease such as Charcot-Marie-Tooth
slots.rationale: Pes cavus concentrates pressure on the heel and metatarsal heads. A new high arch needs a neurologic look.

slots.clue: Swelling graded by pitting and measured by circumference or weight
slots.rationale: Pitting edema is tracked the same way each visit. A sudden increase can be heart failure or a clot.

slots.clue: Cranial nerve VI, which abducts the eye
slots.rationale: Abducens palsy causes a medial resting eye and double vision on lateral gaze. It has a long intracranial course.

slots.clue: Pain felt at a distance from the source, such as hip pain felt in the knee
slots.rationale: Referred pain does not follow a dermatome the way radicular pain does. Screen the joint above and below.

slots.clue: Osteoarthritis index of pain, stiffness, and function
slots.rationale: The WOMAC is common in hip and knee arthritis. It is a patient report, not a strength test.

slots.clue: Knee flexors; most are tibial-nerve innervated
slots.rationale: The short head of biceps femoris is the peroneal exception. Hamstrings also extend the hip.

slots.clue: Score that estimates the probability of deep vein thrombosis
slots.rationale: The Wells criteria sort pretest probability. They do not replace imaging when suspicion is real.

slots.clue: Loss of half the visual field, often homonymous after a stroke
slots.rationale: Homonymous hemianopia is a field cut. Patients turn the head to scan; it is not the same as neglect.

slots.clue: Test for de Quervain tenosynovitis of the thumb tendons
slots.rationale: Finkelstein ulnar-deviates the clenched thumb. Pain over the radial styloid is positive.

slots.clue: Passive glide graded to restore accessory motion
slots.rationale: Joint mobilization grades I and II are for pain. Grades III and IV stretch the capsule.

slots.clue: Drop in pressure on standing that is watched after bed rest
slots.rationale: Orthostatic hypotension is managed with slow rises, compression, and fluid when allowed. It is measured, not assumed.

slots.clue: Embolism that presents with sudden dyspnea after a clot
slots.rationale: Pulmonary embolism is an emergency. Sudden shortness of breath and chest pain after immobility are the story.

slots.clue: Release technique aimed at fascial restriction
slots.rationale: Myofascial release uses sustained pressure. Contraindications include malignancy and anticoagulation caution.

slots.clue: Index of basic activities of daily living
slots.rationale: The Barthel Index scores feeding, bathing, transfers, and mobility. Higher is more independent.
